values.note: Primitive designated sites. Camping only at designated sites; none along the river or on sandbars.

sites.source: https://www.fws.gov/refuge/browns-park/visit-us/activities/camping ('There are 7 campsites at this campground.'; 'Camping inside the Refuge is allowed only at designated sites within these two campgrounds.'; 'Camping along the river and/or on sandbars is prohibited.'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Pit toilets, fire rings, boat ramp and a livestock corral. No trash service: pack it out. Bring firewood (collecting is prohibited). Generators 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. only.

facilities.source: https://www.fws.gov/refuge/browns-park/visit-us/activities/camping ('Amenities include fire rings, pit toilets, a boat ramp, and a livestock corral.'; 'Potable water is not available.'; 'Trash disposal is not provided.'; 'firewood collection within the Refuge is prohibited'; 'the use of generators is only allowed between the hours of 7am to 10pm'), read 2026-10-28

season.source: https://www.fws.gov/refuge/browns-park/visit-us/activities/camping ('The campgrounds and associated facilities are open throughout the year.'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: No reservations; first come, first served. 14 days within any 28.

booking.source: https://www.fws.gov/refuge/browns-park/visit-us/activities/camping ('we do not take campsite reservations; all campsites are first-come first-served to all visitors'; 'Camping is limited to 14 days within a 28-day period.'), read 2026-10-28

note: Browns Park National Wildlife Refuge (USFWS) on the Green River at the west end of the Wildlife Drive, beside the historic single-lane Swinging Bridge (20-ton limit, 8 ft 6 in at its narrowest). Reached by long gravel roads. --Claude
summary: USFWS refuge camping page: confirmed 7 sites, pit toilets, no water, free, FCFS, 14 days in 28, open all year; phone 970-365-3613 confirmed on the refuge home page. Note cleaned of field facts. Riverview kept; pin is in the river.
flags: Bridge: 'The Swinging Bridge is single-lane with a maximum weight capacity of 20 tons, and the narrowest width for vehicles to pass is 8'6".' EKKO (~11,000 lb GVWR) is well under 20 tons; check its mirror-to-mirror width against 8 ft 6 in. The campground is on the north bank, so whether the bridge must be crossed depends on the approach (from CO-318 on the north side it need not be).
Road: the refuge's camping page has no road-surface, RV or trailer wording and no length figure; no closures or alerts on the refuge home page.

Pin: stored 40.82783,-109.03044 is in the middle of the Green River just east of the bridge. The campground loop (pit-toilet building) is on the north bank ~40.8292,-109.0337, ~180 m west-northwest; better pin there.

Waterfront (stored riverview, kept): the Green River here is ~70-90 m wide (river-sized). On imagery the campground loop sits ~50-70 m north of the water behind a band of riverbank brush, with a couple of pull-offs further west ~30-40 m from the bank; the page says the campground 'lies directly along the Green River' but camping 'along the river and/or on sandbars is prohibited'. Riverfront not confirmed at the sites; riverview stands.
hookups (electric 0, water/sewer false) left as stored: the page calls it a 'primitive' campground but states nothing about hookups.
